dek_candidates: What the DRHP discloses about A B Infrabuild Limited's business, offer, financials and risks — sourced to the filing, page by page.
A Mumbai infrastructure contractor and RMC maker plans a 44.28-lakh-share SME IPO. The filing shows a railway-heavy order book, concentrated ownership, and a sharp FY2018 profit jump.

beats.beat: The business sits in two segments: creation of infrastructure, and operation of a ready-mix concrete plant at Thane.

Infrastructure work spans railways (platforms, station buildings, gauge conversion, track laying), bridges (beam, cantilever, arch, suspension, cable-stayed, truss), and roads (bituminous and concrete).

Revenue depends on winning government tenders. The filing describes the cycle: client floats a tender, pre-bid meeting, contractor bids, lowest quote gets the letter of acceptance, contractor deposits a performance guarantee, then site handover.

Clients are mostly government and quasi-government: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation, MMRDA, and Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation, plus private names like Sky Way Infrastructure and Dev Engineers.
The concentration is material: top customers contributed 57% of revenue in FY2018, and Western Railway — a client since 2006 — accounts for 52% of the orders on hand.
The filing claims competitive strengths: cost efficiency, timely delivery, technical expertise, a 'Box Pushing' technique, modern machinery, and a focus on Mumbai while consolidating in Maharashtra.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations fell from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018; FY2014 revenue was ₹86.61 crore.
Net profit after adjustments was just ₹0.16 crore in FY2017 and ₹3.15 crore in FY2018 — a sharp spike after four thin years between ₹0.16 crore and ₹0.96 crore.
Profit before interest, depreciation and tax was ₹9.46 crore in FY2015, ₹6.76 crore in FY2017, and ₹9.29 crore in FY2018.
The balance sheet is short-debt heavy: short-term borrowings were ₹35.37 crore at FY2018 against long-term borrowings of ₹1.33 crore; short-term debt has risen from ₹30.82 crore in FY2014.
Total assets grew from ₹70.62 crore in FY2014 to ₹82.32 crore in FY2018.
The DRHP warns that the company had negative cash flow in recent financial years; the extracted pages do not provide the cash-flow figures themselves.

beats.beat: The promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, Managing Director, holding 74,95,476 equity shares — 90.949% of pre-issue paid-up capital.
The other whole-time directors each hold 300 shares; the CFO, Anchal Pachori, is a 28-year-old Chartered Accountant, and the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer is Mohit Soni.
The digest also records a 9% equity holding by Hatim Sakerwala as on the date of the draft, without explaining how this relates to the promoter's 90.949% holding.

Related-party transactions are disclosed: loan taken from KMP / board of directors of ₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018, director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties of ₹324.3 lakhs as on 31 March 2018.
The filing says no director is on the RBI list of wilful defaulters, no criminal cases are disclosed against directors, and the promoter confirms he is not a wilful defaulter.

Governance flags to note: two promoter-promoted companies were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 for non-operation, and the company issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price.

beats.beat: The construction sector contributes roughly 8% of India's GDP and is highly fragmented and working capital intensive.

The demand drivers named by the filing: government flagship programmes including 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India and Power for All; eased FDI norms in 15 sectors including real estate and construction; urbanisation; rising income and population growth.
The filing cites a ₹50 trillion investment requirement in infrastructure by 2022, and expects logistics sector growth from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020, a 10.5% CAGR.
Broader numbers in the DRHP: GDP growth above 7% in 2017, cumulative core-industries growth of 4.2% in 2017-18, and India's jump to 35th on the World Bank Logistics Performance Index in 2016.
Competition is described as both organised and unorganised. The SWOT section lists slow pace of government projects, working capital crunch, and changes in government policies as the main headwinds.
Regulatory context in the filing: Companies Act 2013, GST, Factories Act 1948, and environmental laws including the Water and Air Pollution Acts and Environment Protection Act.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild is a Mumbai-based infrastructure construction and ready-mix concrete business. It builds railway, bridge and road projects for government clients and runs an RMC plant at Kashimira, Thane.
The company is going public on the SME Board with 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each; the issue price is to be determined.
The money raised is earmarked for working capital — ₹1,130 lakhs — and general corporate purposes, the amount of which is not disclosed.
The filing's central tension: revenue has fallen sharply over five years, profit jumped only in FY2018, and a single customer group — Indian Railways — drives more than half the revenue.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader in one breath: who this company is, what it does, what it is raising, and the central tension an investor should hold on to.

beats.beat: The offer is 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at an issue price to be determined.
Lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
Use of proceeds is stated as: to meet working capital requirements, ₹1,130 lakhs, and general corporate purposes, amount to be determined.
The extracted pages do not disclose whether any of the 44.28 lakh shares are an offer for sale, and no selling shareholder is named; the digest presents the issue only as equity shares offered.
The filing says no monitoring agency has been appointed; the audit committee will monitor deployment of funds at management and board discretion.

offer.heading: The offer
offer.purpose: State the issue size, who is managing it, what the money is for, and what the filing has not disclosed about the offer structure.

beats.beat: Revenue is pinned to Indian Railways: it was the largest customer with 57% of FY2018 revenue; losing or reducing that relationship would cut revenues significantly.
The business model depends on winning government tenders; if most bids are not accepted or are won at lower values, results will be directly hit.
Cash flow is already negative in recent financial years, receivables may not be recovered on time, and unsecured loans of ₹405.02 lakhs were repayable on demand as of March 31, 2018.
The order book is not a guarantee of revenue: contracts can be adjusted, cancelled or suspended by clients, and cost overruns can erase profits.
Governance overhang: the company has entered into related-party transactions and may continue to do so, and promoter-linked companies were struck off by the ROC in 2016 for non-operation.

risks.heading: The five material risks
risks.purpose: Give the reader the specific, company-level risks that matter most, each grounded in the filing.

beats.beat: The face value is ₹10 and the issue price is to be determined; the DRHP says the price will be justified against accounting ratios.

The Basis for Issue Price section on page 54 lists several ratio values — including 12.59 and 28.14 for FY2017-18 — but the digest does not preserve the table's column labels, so the values cannot be safely mapped to EPS, NAV or RoNW.

The filing includes a 'Comparison of Accounting Ratios with Peer Group Companies' on page 55, but the digest captures only two figures — 12.39 and 44.71 — without naming the peers or labelling the ratios.
Because the peer names and ratio labels are missing, no peer P/E table and no implied price range can be constructed from this digest.
